approach.title: Approach
approach.intro: Psychology and data share a problem: measuring things you can’t observe directly. Three ideas from psychometrics I apply to every pipeline.

validity.label: Validity
validity.title: Does it measure what it claims to?
validity.text: “Active users” can mean whoever opened the app or whoever did something in it. Before building a metric I write down which behavior it has to capture and check it against real cases.

reliability.label: Reliability
reliability.title: Same input, same result
reliability.text: A pipeline that runs twice has to return the same number. Idempotent loads, tests and versioned sources: if a value changes, it should be because what it measures changed.

goodhart.label: Goodhart
goodhart.title: When the metric becomes the target
goodhart.text: A number people chase stops measuring what it used to. So every key metric comes with another one that keeps it honest: sales alongside returns, speed alongside errors.

about.title: From backend to data.
about.intro: Today I build APIs and databases; what I want to build is pipelines.
about.photoAlt: Marcos Rio holding a mate in the snowy mountains of Mendoza.
bio: I’ve been a developer at a software company since 2024. My day-to-day work revolves around databases: modeling in PostgreSQL, migrations, SQL for reporting and, lately, AI integration so analytics can be queried in natural language.

I’m looking for my first role as a data engineer and, in the meantime, I build practice projects. Before and alongside that I taught: seven years at a technical secondary school and classes in the Psychology degree, where I’m finishing my thesis.

points: Designed the platform’s relational data model in PostgreSQL.
ETL processes to migrate data from a legacy system, preserving referential integrity.
Business metrics in SQL (CTEs, window functions) for reports and dashboards, defined with the teams that use them.
Semantic search with pgvector and tool-calling agents.
Currently: AI integration for chat and natural-language queries over analytics and dashboards.
